pages.text: Specification number: 101000   Version Date:   04-02-2021  Dutch Unsalted Lactic Butter (82%)  Ongezouten zure boter (82%) Mildgesäuerte Markenbutter (82%) Beurre lactique non salé (82%)  Page:   1 of   3  Product description  Dutch unsalted lactic churned butter (min. 82% milk fat), obtained from fresh cream, with a moderately firm to firm texture.  Foil- wrapped packaging of 125, 200, 250, 400, 500 and 1000 g℮;  3D butter 10 0 g℮ for holidays;  Cartons 5000 g℮.  Different sizes on request.  Ingredients (suggested labelling according to Regulation (EU) No. 1169/2011)*  Butter (min. 82% MILK fat)  * Country regulations for product labelling vary. Royal VIVBuisman advises customers to check local regulations to determine correct labelling of this ingredient.  Sensorial data  Colour: light yellow to yellow   Texture: moderately firm to firm   Flavour: buttery  Chemical/physical data  Method derived from  Milk fat content   min.   82.0   %   NEN-EN-ISO 3727-3  Moisture   max.   16.0   %   NEN-EN-ISO 3727-1  Non-fat milk solids   max.   2.0   %   NEN-EN-ISO 3727-2  Free fatty acids   max.   0.3   % as oleic acid   NEN-ISO 1740  pH of milk phase   4.5   -   5.3   NEN 3736  Microbiological data  Method derived from  Total plate count (non-lactic)   <   <10.000   cfu/g   NEN-EN-ISO 4833  Yeasts and moulds   <   <500   cfu/g   NEN-ISO 21527-1  Enterobacteriaceae   <   <10   cfu/g   NEN-ISO 21528-2  Salmonella*   Absent   in 25 g   NEN-EN-ISO 6579  Listeria monocytogenes*   <100   cfu/g   NEN-EN-ISO 11290-1  Staphylococcus aureus*   Absent   in 1 g   NEN-EN-ISO 6888-2  *based on monitoring  Storage conditions and maximum shelf life  Temperature   ≤   -18 °C   ≤ 6 °C  Foil wrapped   1 year   85 days  3D butter   Depends on holiday   45 days  Cartons 5000 g   2 years   100 days  Shelf life is guaranteed for unopened packaging, provided that the product is stored dry, odour free, dark and out of direct sunlight. It is recommended to use the product shortly after opening.  The cutoms code of the 25kg butter is: 0405 1019.

Dutch Dairy Regulations  Supervision of compliance with legislation and regulations in Dutch dairy production: The Dutch government supervises the safety and quality - of products and production processes - throughout the entire supply chain. Supervisory guidelines are based on Dutch and European legislation and regulations. A number of official authorities carry out the inspections, including the Netherlands Controlling Authority of Milk and Milk Products (COKZ), the Inspection Service of Public Health and Veterinary Aspects and the Animal Feed Sector Quality Service and the National Inspection Service of Livestock and Meat.

Specification number: 101000   Version Date:   04-02-2021  Dutch Unsalted Lactic Butter (82%)  Ongezouten zure boter (82%) Mildgesäuerte Markenbutter (82%) Beurre lactique non salé (82%)  Page:   3 of   3  Statement Contaminants and residues  We, Royal VIVBuisman, herewith declare that our products are in compliance with Commission Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006, Regulation (EC) No 396/2005 and Council Regulation (EEC) No 470/2009 and their amendments regarding contaminants, residues of pesticides and residues of veterinary medicinal products. These parameters are under supervision of the Netherlands Controlling Authority for Milk and Milk products (COKZ).  Statement Ionising radiation treatment / irradiation  We, Royal VIVBuisman, herewith declare that our products are not treated with ionising radiation/irradiation as mentioned in Directive 1999/2/EC and Directive 1999/3/EC.  To the best of our knowledge and based on statements of our suppliers, we herewith also declare that our products do not contain any ingredients, which are treated with ionising radiation/irradiation.  This statement does not take into account the packaging of the product.  EU legislations  Packaging   In accordance with Regulation (EC) No 1935/2004, Commission Regulation (EC) No 2023/2006, Commission Regulation (EU) No 10/2011 and its amendments.  Food hygiene   In accordance with Regulation (EC) No 852/2004, Regulation (EC) No 853/2004 and Regulation (EC) No 854/2004 and their amendments.  Food safety   In accordance with Regulation (EC) No 178/2002 and its amendments.  Radioactivity   In accordance with Council Regulation (Euratom) No 2016/52 and its amendments.
